claim: Commissural connections unifying hemispheric sensory representations of vision and touch occur in cortex.
source: Connections unifying hemispheric sensory representations of vision and touch occur in cortex, but for hearing, commissural connections earlier in the pathway may be important.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about sensory systems.

claim: For hearing, commissural connections earlier in the pathway may be important.
source: Connections unifying hemispheric sensory representations of vision and touch occur in cortex, but for hearing, commissural connections earlier in the pathway may be important.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the auditory system.

claim: The brainstem auditory pathways course bilaterally to the inferior colliculi (ICs).
source: The brainstem auditory pathways course bilaterally to the inferior colliculi (ICs).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about the auditory system.

claim: Each IC represents one side of auditory space.
source: Each IC represents one side of auditory space but they are interconnected by a commissure.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IC function.

claim: The ICs are interconnected by a commissure.
source: Each IC represents one side of auditory space but they are interconnected by a commissure.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Deactivating one IC in guinea pig with cooling or microdialysis of procaine influences fundamental aspects of auditory processing in the other IC.
source: By deactivating one IC in guinea pig with cooling or microdialysis of procaine, and recording neural activity to sound in the other, we found that commissural input influences fundamental aspects of auditory processing.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data from the study.

claim: The areas of nonV frequency response areas (FRAs) were modulated by commissural input.
source: The areas of nonV frequency response areas (FRAs) were modulated, but the areas of almost all V-shaped FRAs were not.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: The areas of almost all V-shaped FRAs were not modulated by commissural input.
source: The areas of nonV frequency response areas (FRAs) were modulated, but the areas of almost all V-shaped FRAs were not.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: The supra-threshold sensitivity of rate level functions decreased during deactivation of the contralateral IC.
source: The supra-threshold sensitivity of rate level functions decreased during deactivation and the ability to signal changes in sound level was decremented.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: The ability to signal changes in sound level was decremented during deactivation of the contralateral IC.
source: The supra-threshold sensitivity of rate level functions decreased during deactivation and the ability to signal changes in sound level was decremented.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: The ICs should be viewed as a single entity in which the representation of sound in each is governed by the other.
source: This commissural enhancement suggests the ICs should be viewed as a single entity in which the representation of sound in each is governed by the other.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Vision and touch have functional interaction between the two sides of the pathway occurring in the cerebral cortex predominantly via the corpus callosum.
source: Generation of a unified representation of sensory space requires a functional interaction between the two sides of the pathway, which, in the case of vision and touch, occurs in the cerebral cortex predominantly via the corpus callosum.
evidence: This is established knowledge about sensory systems.

claim: Hearing is distinct amongst the senses in having extensive pre-thalamic processing in the brainstem.
source: Hearing, however, is distinct amongst the senses in having extensive pre-thalamic processing in the brainstem.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the auditory system.

claim: The fundamental properties of sound frequency and level are influenced by extensive interactions between the left and right sides of the pathway at the brainstem level.
source: Here we report evidence demonstrating that the fundamental properties of sound frequency and level are influenced by extensive interactions between the left and right sides of the pathway at this more peripheral level.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: The sub-thalamic auditory system consists of chains of nuclei in the brainstem giving rise to multiple parallel pathways represented in mirror image about the midline.
source: The sub-thalamic auditory system consists of chains of nuclei in the brainstem giving rise to multiple parallel pathways represented in mirror image about the midline.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Processing in each side of the auditory pathway is dominated by the respective contralateral sound field.
source: Processing in each side is dominated by the respective contralateral sound field.
evidence: This is established knowledge about auditory processing.

claim: Each limb of the auditory pathway culminates in the midbrain in the respective left or right inferior colliculi (ICs).
source: Each limb of the pathway culminates in the midbrain in the respective left or right inferior colliculi (ICs) whose outputs provide the primary ascending input to the auditory thalamus and cortex on each side.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The outputs of the ICs provide the primary ascending input to the auditory thalamus and cortex on each side.
source: Each limb of the pathway culminates in the midbrain in the respective left or right inferior colliculi (ICs) whose outputs provide the primary ascending input to the auditory thalamus and cortex on each side.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The left and right auditory pathways involve crossed connections at several levels.
source: While the left and right pathways are distinct, they involve crossed connections at several levels (Moore and Osen, 1979; Glendenning and Masterton, 1983; Glendenning et al., 1985; Oliver, 2000; Cant and Benson, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Crossed connections between the cochlear nuclei and the superior olivary complex mediate interactions that extract the interaural disparities underlying sound localization.
source: Some of these crossed connections, such as those between the cochlear nuclei and the superior olivary complex, occur between different levels in the hierarchy and mediate interactions that extract the interaural disparities underlying sound localization.
evidence: This is established knowledge about auditory processing.

claim: Crossed connections between the cochlear nuclei and the superior olivary complex have been termed the acoustic chiasm.
source: Such connections have been termed the acoustic chiasm (Glendenning et al., 1985).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Commissural connections interconnect mirror opposite nuclei in the auditory pathway.
source: In addition, there are commissural connections that interconnect mirror opposite nuclei.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Commissural connections are found as early in the auditory pathway as the cochlear nuclei.
source: These are found as early in the pathway as the cochlear nuclei (Adams and Warr, 1976; Cant and Gaston, 1982), while, in the midbrain, the commissure of Probst connects the dorsal nuclei of the lateral lemniscus (DNLLs) (Goldberg and Moore, 1967; Hutson et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The commissure of Probst connects the dorsal nuclei of the lateral lemniscus (DNLLs).
source: These are found as early in the pathway as the cochlear nuclei (Adams and Warr, 1976; Cant and Gaston, 1982), while, in the midbrain, the commissure of Probst connects the dorsal nuclei of the lateral lemniscus (DNLLs) (Goldberg and Moore, 1967; Hutson et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The commissure of the inferior colliculus (CoIC) is the most prominent commissural connection in the auditory pathway.
source: But the most prominent of these connections is the commissure of the inferior colliculus (CoIC) (Beyerl, 1978; Adams, 1980; Aitkin and Phillips, 1984; Coleman and Clerici, 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The CoIC interconnects the ICs in a systematic fashion that mirrors the spatial representation of frequency (tonotopicity) in these nuclei.
source: The CoIC interconnects the ICs in a systematic fashion that mirrors the spatial representation of frequency (tonotopicity) in these nuclei (Adams, 1980; González-Hernández et al., 1986; Saldaña and Merchán, 1992; Malmierca et al., 1995, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CoIC fibers are predominantly excitatory.
source: These fibers are predominantly excitatory although a significant minority (∼10–20%) are GABAergic (González-Hernández et al., 1996; Hernández et al., 2006; Nakamoto et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A significant minority (∼10–20%) of CoIC fibers are GABAergic.
source: These fibers are predominantly excitatory although a significant minority (∼10–20%) are GABAergic (González-Hernández et al., 1996; Hernández et al., 2006; Nakamoto et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The commissure of the inferior colliculus is the final point of interaction between the two limbs of the ascending auditory pathway prior to the auditory cortex.
source: This commissure is the final point of interaction between the two limbs of the ascending auditory pathway prior to the auditory cortex.
evidence: This is an inference based on anatomical knowledge.

claim: Recent in vivo studies in the IC have led to speculation that the CoIC may mediate binaural processing between the ICs.
source: Recent in vivo studies in the IC in response to sound stimuli that were varied in azimuthal location have led to the speculation that the CoIC may mediate binaural processing between the ICs (Malmierca et al., 2005; Li and Pollak, 2013; Ono and Oliver, 2014).
evidence: This is speculation based on cited previous studies.

claim: Extracellular recordings were made from 125 single units in the right IC in response to diotic pure tones.
source: To investigate the influence of the CoIC on auditory processing we made extracellular recordings from 125 single units in the right IC in response to diotic pure tones to generate frequency response areas (FRAs) (LeBeau et al., 2001) and rate level functions (RLFs) (Rees and Palmer, 1988).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology and data collection.

claim: Recordings were made before, during and after deactivation of the left IC using either cryoloop cooling or microdialysis of procaine in anesthetized adult guinea pigs.
source: Recordings were made before, during and after deactivation of the left IC using either cryoloop cooling (Orton et al., 2012) or microdialysis of procaine (MDP) in anesthetized adult guinea pigs.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: The cryoloop abolished or reduced firing rates in the dorsal half of one IC (to the depth at which frequencies of up to ∼8 kHz are represented in the tonotopic sequence) while leaving ventral regions less affected.
source: We have demonstrated that the cryoloop in our implementation abolished or reduced firing rates in the dorsal half of one IC (to the depth at which frequencies of up to ∼8 kHz are represented in the tonotopic sequence) while leaving ventral regions less affected.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: Cooling did not spread to the contralateral IC.
source: Cooling did not spread to the contralateral IC and did not modulate the afferent volley to the contralateral IC, showing that changes imparted by the cooling protocol in the contralateral IC were of commissural origin (Orton et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from a cited study.

claim: Cooling did not modulate the afferent volley to the contralateral IC.
source: Cooling did not spread to the contralateral IC and did not modulate the afferent volley to the contralateral IC, showing that changes imparted by the cooling protocol in the contralateral IC were of commissural origin (Orton et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from a cited study.

claim: Changes imparted by the cooling protocol in the contralateral IC were of commissural origin.
source: Cooling did not spread to the contralateral IC and did not modulate the afferent volley to the contralateral IC, showing that changes imparted by the cooling protocol in the contralateral IC were of commissural origin (Orton et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from a cited study.

claim: Procaine caused an immediate and persistent deactivation of multi-unit activity throughout infusion.
source: Procaine caused an immediate and persistent deactivation throughout infusion.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: After switching back to aCSF, firing recovered to near control levels after 20 min.
source: After switching back to aCSF, firing recovered to near control levels after 20 min.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Procaine infusion abolished firing at virtually all frequencies and levels in the multi-unit FRA.
source: Procaine infusion abolished firing at virtually all frequencies and levels.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: After 20 min of aCSF washout the response area returned to control.
source: After 20 min of aCSF washout the response area returned to control.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Insertion of the microdialysis probe into the left IC produced negligible trauma.
source: Insertion of the microdialysis probe into the left IC produced negligible trauma.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: Lesions caused by the microdialysis probe comprised just 1.49% (±0.31) of the area of the IC.
source: Lesions comprised just 1.49% (±0.31) of the area of the IC.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from histological measurements.

claim: Procaine has a high pKa and consequently has low efficacy in vivo compared to other sodium channel blockers.
source: While procaine has a high pKa, and consequently has low efficacy in vivo compared to other sodium channel blockers that are commonly used in deactivation studies (Truant and Takman, 1959), recovery from deactivation is faster than with amide local anesthetics such as lidocaine (Sung and Truant, 1954) as ester local anesthetics are metabolized in plasma rather than liver (Covino, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Recovery from procaine deactivation is faster than with amide local anesthetics such as lidocaine.
source: While procaine has a high pKa, and consequently has low efficacy in vivo compared to other sodium channel blockers that are commonly used in deactivation studies (Truant and Takman, 1959), recovery from deactivation is faster than with amide local anesthetics such as lidocaine (Sung and Truant, 1954) as ester local anesthetics are metabolized in plasma rather than liver (Covino, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Ester local anesthetics are metabolized in plasma rather than liver.
source: While procaine has a high pKa, and consequently has low efficacy in vivo compared to other sodium channel blockers that are commonly used in deactivation studies (Truant and Takman, 1959), recovery from deactivation is faster than with amide local anesthetics such as lidocaine (Sung and Truant, 1954) as ester local anesthetics are metabolized in plasma rather than liver (Covino, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Procaine has no effect on resting membrane potential.
source: Procaine has no effect of resting membrane potential (Taylor, 1959) or spike amplitude (Butterworth and Cole, 1990).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Procaine has no effect on spike amplitude.
source: Procaine has no effect of resting membrane potential (Taylor, 1959) or spike amplitude (Butterworth and Cole, 1990).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Microdialysis of procaine rapidly deactivated neurons without producing the mechanical disturbances associated with pressure injection.
source: Microdialysis of procaine rapidly deactivated neurons without producing the mechanical disturbances associated with pressure injection (Malmierca et al., 2003, 2005).
evidence: This is based on experimental data and comparison to cited previous studies.

claim: Frequency response areas in the IC can be grouped as being either V-shaped or into a more heterogeneous group collectively termed nonV.
source: Frequency response areas in the IC are diverse; however, they can be grouped as being either V-shaped, with responses similar to those found in the in the auditory nerve, or into a more heterogeneous group collectively termed nonV.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IC responses.

claim: V-shaped FRAs have responses similar to those found in the auditory nerve.
source: Frequency response areas in the IC are diverse; however, they can be grouped as being either V-shaped, with responses similar to those found in the in the auditory nerve, or into a more heterogeneous group collectively termed nonV.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IC responses.

claim: At least seven response area types can be defined within the nonV group.
source: At least seven response area types can be defined within this group, but they represent points on a continuum rather than discrete classes (Palmer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: NonV response area types represent points on a continuum rather than discrete classes.
source: At least seven response area types can be defined within this group, but they represent points on a continuum rather than discrete classes (Palmer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Similar effects were found in response to either cooling or MDP deactivation of the contralateral IC.
source: Similar effects were found in response to either cooling or MDP deactivation of the contralateral IC.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: Control units tested with cooling or MDP did not differ in characteristic frequency (CF), FRA area or firing rate.
source: Control units tested with cooling or MDP did not differ in characteristic frequency (CF), FRA area or firing rate.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: The area of V FRAs did not change in response to either cooling (n = 37) or MDP (n = 12) deactivation of the contralateral IC.
source: The area of V FRAs did not change in response to either cooling (n = 37) or MDP (n = 12) deactivation of the contralateral IC.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Changes in firing rate within and across the existing response area occurred for most V FRAs in response to cooling and MDP deactivation.
source: Conversely, changes in firing rate within and across the existing response area occurred for most V FRAs in response to cooling and MDP deactivation.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Both increases and decreases in firing rate were seen in the population of V FRAs and these recovered towards control levels after deactivation was stopped.
source: Both increases and decreases in firing rate were seen in the population and these recovered towards control levels after deactivation was stopped.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: 14% (7/49) of V FRAs decreased in firing rate by more than 20%.
source: With a 20% change in firing rate as a criterion of change (LeBeau et al., 2001, Burger and Pollak, 2001; Park et al., 2008), 14% (7/49) V FRAs decreased in firing rate while 35% (17/49) increased.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: 35% (17/49) of V FRAs increased in firing rate by more than 20%.
source: With a 20% change in firing rate as a criterion of change (LeBeau et al., 2001, Burger and Pollak, 2001; Park et al., 2008), 14% (7/49) V FRAs decreased in firing rate while 35% (17/49) increased.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: FRAs in the nonV group showed dramatic changes in area following deactivation of the other IC.
source: In contrast to V FRAs, FRAs in the nonV group showed dramatic changes in area following deactivation of the other IC (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: A low-tilt FRA declined in both spontaneous and auditory driven firing rate and its FRA reduced in area by 52% during procaine deactivation.
source: For example, the neuron whose low-tilt FRA is shown in Figure 3A declined in both spontaneous and auditory driven firing rate and its FRA reduced in area by 52% (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: A narrow FRA type reduced in area by 86% during cooling deactivation.
source: The narrow FRA type in Figure 3D reduced in area by 86% (Figure 3E) and the closed FRA in Figure 3G expanded in area by 234% (Figure 3H) and showed an elevation in firing rate for frequencies centered on its CF, the frequency to which it was most sensitive.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3D-E.

claim: A closed FRA expanded in area by 234% and showed an elevation in firing rate for frequencies centered on its CF during cooling deactivation.
source: The narrow FRA type in Figure 3D reduced in area by 86% (Figure 3E) and the closed FRA in Figure 3G expanded in area by 234% (Figure 3H) and showed an elevation in firing rate for frequencies centered on its CF, the frequency to which it was most sensitive.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3G-H.

claim: A broad FRA reduced in area by 40% during cooling deactivation.
source: The broad FRA in Figure 3J reduced in area by 40% (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3J-K.

claim: All changes in nonV FRAs reversed to near control levels on recovery.
source: All of these changes reversed to near control levels on recovery (Figure 3C,F,I,L).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The firing rate of 34% (17/50) of nonV FRAs decreased during deactivation.
source: Quantitative analysis found that the firing rate of 34% (17/50) of nonV FRAs decreased in firing rate while 28% (14/50) increased.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: The firing rate of 28% (14/50) of nonV FRAs increased during deactivation.
source: Quantitative analysis found that the firing rate of 34% (17/50) of nonV FRAs decreased in firing rate while 28% (14/50) increased.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: The distributions of change in firing rate for both V and nonV FRAs were similar.
source: The distributions of change in firing rate for both V and nonV FRAs (Figure 4B) were similar (two sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: D(97) = 0.20; p = 0.26).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The range of changes in nonV FRAs was more than double that of V FRAs.
source: There was a difference between the change in area for the two FRA classes. The distribution of V FRA areas was almost unchanged during deactivation (Figure 4C), but the range of changes in nonV FRAs was more than double that of V FRAs (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: NonV FRAs were modulated more than V FRAs in terms of area change.
source: Comparison of FRA area change between V and nonV FRAs showed that nonV FRAs were modulated more than V (D(97) = 0.32; p = 0.009).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Non-monotonic RLFs comprised 12 of the 38 neurons recorded.
source: Non-monotonic RLFs comprised 12 of the 38 neurons recorded.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: Only non-monotonic RLFs changed shape during contralateral IC deactivation.
source: While examples of all RLF types showed firing rate changes during contralateral IC deactivation, only non-monotonic RLFs changed shape.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: Four of the 12 non-monotonic RLFs became monotonic during deactivation.
source: Four of the 12 non-monotonic RLFs became monotonic (Figure 5A,C), four became straight (Figure 5B), while the remainder remained non-monotonic.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Four of the 12 non-monotonic RLFs became straight during deactivation.
source: Four of the 12 non-monotonic RLFs became monotonic (Figure 5A,C), four became straight (Figure 5B), while the remainder remained non-monotonic.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: A Fisher's exact test found that the probability of the observed distribution of RLF type changes occurring or one more extreme was 0.0002.
source: A Fisher's exact test found that the probability of the observed distribution occurring or one more extreme, was 0.0002.
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Non-monotonic RLFs in IC are a distinct type of RLF whose shape can be formed by CoIC processing.
source: Thus, non-monotonic RLFs in IC are a distinct type of RLF whose shape can be formed by CoIC processing.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: In the majority of units, deactivation shifted RLFs so that a higher sound level was required to evoke the half maximum firing rate than in the control condition.
source: In the majority of units, deactivation shifted RLFs so that a higher sound level was required to evoke the half maximum firing rate than in the control condition (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5D-F.

claim: On recovery, the half maximum firing rate of RLFs returned to values similar to the control condition.
source: On recovery, the half maximum firing rate of these RLFs returned to values similar to the control condition.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: The median sound level required to elicit half maximal firing increased from 50.9 dB SPL (95% CI: 46.1 56.2) to 59.3 dB SPL (95% CI: 55.2 65.0) on deactivation.
source: In the population of RLFs (Figure 5G) the median sound level required to elicit half maximal firing increased from 50.9 dB sound pressure level (SPL) (95% CI: 46.1 56.2) to 59.3 dB SPL (95% CI: 55.2 65.0) on deactivation.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: On recovery, the median half maximal level of the distribution returned to 51.3 dB SPL (95% CI: 47.5 61.1).
source: On recovery, the median half maximal level of the distribution returned to 51.3 dB SPL (95% CI: 47.5 61.1).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: CoIC rescaling improved supra-threshold coding of sound level.
source: The increase in sound level required to reach half maximal firing rate during deactivation indicated that CoIC rescaling improved supra-threshold coding of sound level (Friedman repeated measures ANOVA on ranks: χ2(2) = 12.72; p = 0.001).
evidence: This is an inference based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: A higher sound level was required to elicit half maximum firing during contralateral IC deactivation than during control recordings.
source: Post hoc analysis found a higher sound level was required to elicit half maximum firing during contralateral IC deactivation than during control recordings (Z = −3.94; p = 0.00008).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: There was no difference between the level required to evoke half maximal firing in the control and recovery conditions.
source: There was no difference between the level required to evoke half maximal firing in the control and recovery conditions (Z = −1.41; p = 0.15).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: There was no correlation between the change in threshold and the change in half maximum firing.
source: There was no correlation between the change in threshold and the change in half maximum firing (rs(14) = 0.20; p = 0.45).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The predominant effect of removing CoIC input was to rescale supra-threshold responses, consistent with the operation of a gain control of neuronal output.
source: This demonstrates that the predominant effect of removing CoIC input was to rescale supra-threshold responses, consistent with the operation of a gain control of neuronal output.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: The median DI for the population of RLFs in the control condition was 1.72 (95% CI: 1.52 1.99).
source: For the 38 units, the population DIs in the control condition (median = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.52 1.99) were reduced during contralateral IC deactivation (median = 1.54; 95% CI: 1.37 1.68) although some units did show an elevation (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The median DI for the population of RLFs was reduced to 1.54 (95% CI: 1.37 1.68) during contralateral IC deactivation.
source: For the 38 units, the population DIs in the control condition (median = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.52 1.99) were reduced during contralateral IC deactivation (median = 1.54; 95% CI: 1.37 1.68) although some units did show an elevation (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Deactivating the contralateral IC reduced the distribution of DIs.
source: Deactivating the contralateral IC reduced the distribution of DIs (Wilcoxon signed rank test: Z = −2.18; p = 0.028).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The supra-threshold gain control which the CoIC exerts over IC responses enhances the ability of IC neurons to discriminate changes in sound level.
source: Such changes demonstrate that the supra-threshold gain control which the CoIC exerts over IC responses enhances the ability of IC neurons to discriminate changes in sound level.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: Neuronal responses and the formation of receptive fields in the auditory midbrain depend on interactions between the bilateral limbs of the auditory pathway.
source: Our results show that neuronal responses and the formation of receptive fields in the auditory midbrain depend on interactions between the bilateral limbs of the auditory pathway.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all experimental data.

claim: Activity mediated by commissural fibers connecting the ICs influences the responses of almost all the IC neurons recorded in at least one of four ways.
source: Specifically, activity mediated by commissural fibers connecting the ICs influences the responses of almost all the IC neurons we recorded in at least one of four ways.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on experimental data.

claim: The majority of neurons in the sample showed changes in firing rate following deactivation of the other IC.
source: The majority of neurons in our sample showed changes in firing rate following deactivation of the other IC (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Neurons with nonV frequency response areas showed changes in receptive field shape, often (but not exclusively) becoming more V-like in the absence of commissural input.
source: Neurons with nonV frequency response areas also showed changes in receptive field shape, often (but not exclusively) becoming more V-like in the absence of commissural input (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Deactivating inputs from the opposite IC reduced supra-threshold firing rates to sounds of varying level.
source: We observed that deactivating inputs from the opposite IC reduced supra-threshold firing rates to sounds of varying level (Figure 5).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Deactivation reduced the ability of IC neurons to signal changes in sound level by changes in firing rate.
source: Finally, deactivation reduced the ability of IC neurons to signal changes in sound level by changes in firing rate (Figure 6).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Similar changes were observed whether the IC was deactivated by cooling or MDP.
source: Similar changes were observed whether the IC was deactivated by cooling or MDP.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: The anatomical basis for the physiological observations is the CoIC, which tracer experiments demonstrate interconnect the frequency-band laminae in the IC.
source: The anatomical basis for these physiological observations is the CoIC, which tracer experiments demonstrate interconnect the frequency-band laminae in the IC (González-Hernández et al., 1986; Saldaña and Merchán, 1992; Malmierca et al., 1995, 2009).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and cited anatomical studies.

claim: The majority of commissural fibers are excitatory, with only 10–20% labelling for the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA.
source: Immunohistochemical studies suggest that the majority of commissural fibers are excitatory, with only 10–20% labelling for the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA (González-Hernández et al., 1996; Hernández et al., 2006; Nakamoto et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The changes in response properties observed are consistent with commissural input exerting both excitatory and inhibitory influences, with much greater inhibition than would be predicted from the ratio of excitatory to inhibitory fibers.
source: The changes in response properties we observed are consistent with commissural input exerting both excitatory and inhibitory influences, with much greater inhibition than would be predicted from the ratio of excitatory to inhibitory fibers.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and anatomical knowledge.

claim: Within the contralateral IC, excitatory commissural fibers can exert their effects di- or poly-synaptically via inhibitory neurons in the target IC.
source: This suggests that within the contralateral IC, excitatory commissural fibers can exert their effects di- or poly-synaptically via inhibitory neurons in the target IC.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: Evidence supporting di-synaptic inhibition comes from intracellular recordings in IC slices in which electrical stimulation of the CoIC revealed inhibitory currents that were reduced by glutamatergic blockade.
source: Evidence supporting this idea comes from intracellular recordings in IC slices in which electrical stimulation of the CoIC revealed inhibitory currents that were reduced by glutamatergic blockade consistent with di-synaptic inhibition (Smith, 1992; Moore et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: V FRAs have many features in common with the responses of the primary fibers that emerge from the cochlea.
source: Of the two major classes, V FRAs have many features in common with the responses of the primary fibers that emerge from the cochlea.
evidence: This is established knowledge about auditory responses.

claim: Unlike primary fibers, V FRA neurons do receive inhibitory inputs, but this inhibition does not change receptive field shape.
source: However, unlike primary fibers, these neurons do receive inhibitory inputs, but this inhibition does not change receptive field shape (Egorova et al., 2001; Alkhatib et al., 2006; Palmer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The increases in firing rate seen within V response areas are similar to those obtained by iontophoretic blockade of GABA and glycine receptors in IC.
source: The increases in firing rate seen here within V response areas are similar to those obtained by iontophoretic blockade of GABA and glycine receptors in IC (Vater et al., 1992; Yang et al., 1992; LeBeau et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Commissural input serves to rescale the output of neurons with V-shaped responses areas by modifying the balance of local excitation and inhibition without changing area of the receptive field.
source: Commissural input serves to rescale the output of neurons with V-shaped responses areas by modifying the balance of local excitation and inhibition without changing area of the receptive field (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: NonV receptive fields are more heterogeneous in appearance than V receptive fields.
source: In contrast, nonV receptive fields are more heterogeneous in appearance, and although different classes can be identified, many appear to be intermediate types supporting the existence of continua rather than discrete groups (Palmer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: All nonV responses appear to be shaped from V responses by excitatory and/or inhibitory inputs.
source: Nevertheless all nonV responses are similar in appearing to be shaped from V responses by excitatory and/or inhibitory inputs.
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge of auditory processing.

claim: Whether the shaping of nonV responses occurs in the inferior colliculus or is inherited from earlier stages of the auditory pathway is still contentious.
source: Whether this shaping occurs in the inferior colliculus or is inherited from earlier stages of the auditory pathway is still contentious.
evidence: This acknowledges uncertainty in the field.

claim: The contralateral IC is directly or indirectly a source of the inhibitory input that generates nonV receptive fields.
source: The changes in receptive field shape and firing rate we observed on deactivation of the other IC show that it is directly or indirectly a source of the inhibitory input that generates these receptive fields.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: Increasing diversity of spectral responses is a feature of the ascending auditory pathway that presumably reflects the increasing complexity of analyses performed at each level in the process of signal extraction.
source: Increasing diversity of spectral responses is a feature of the ascending auditory pathway that presumably reflects the increasing complexity of analyses performed at each level in the process of signal extraction.
evidence: This is established knowledge about auditory processing.

claim: There is a greater diversity of FRA types in midbrain than in the brainstem.
source: There is a greater diversity of FRA types in midbrain than in the brainstem (Evans and Nelson, 1973; Hernández et al., 2005; Ingham et al., 2006; Palmer et al., 2013) and other types not described in sub-thalamic nuclei are reported in auditory cortex (Shamma et al., 1993; Recanzone et al., 2000; Bitterman et al., 2008; Bartlett et al., 2011; Atencio et al., 2012; Grimsley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: FRA types not described in sub-thalamic nuclei are reported in auditory cortex.
source: There is a greater diversity of FRA types in midbrain than in the brainstem (Evans and Nelson, 1973; Hernández et al., 2005; Ingham et al., 2006; Palmer et al., 2013) and other types not described in sub-thalamic nuclei are reported in auditory cortex (Shamma et al., 1993; Recanzone et al., 2000; Bitterman et al., 2008; Bartlett et al., 2011; Atencio et al., 2012; Grimsley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Lateral connections between the two sides of the auditory pathway play an important role in shaping response areas in the IC, and thus increasing response-type diversity.
source: We have demonstrated that lateral connections between the two sides of the auditory pathway play an important role in shaping response areas in the IC, and thus increasing response-type diversity.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: Commissural input contributes to the non-monotonicity observed in many rate level functions.
source: The analysis of input-output functions for sound level shows that commissural input contributes to the non-monotonicity observed in many of these functions (Figure 5A–C), as well as to the rescaling of responses that enhances the discriminability of sound level in the responses of IC neurons (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Commissural input contributes to the rescaling of responses that enhances the discriminability of sound level in the responses of IC neurons.
source: The analysis of input-output functions for sound level shows that commissural input contributes to the non-monotonicity observed in many of these functions (Figure 5A–C), as well as to the rescaling of responses that enhances the discriminability of sound level in the responses of IC neurons (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The ubiquity of the commissural influence on firing rates supports the contention that the IC exerts an element of gain control on its contralateral counterpart.
source: The ubiquity of the commissural influence on firing rates supports the contention that the IC exerts an element of gain control on its contralateral counterpart (Malmierca et al., 2003, 2005).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and cited previous studies.

claim: The commissure may operate to calibrate one IC with the other.
source: Given that a congruent representation of the auditory environment is dependent on combining the contralateral auditory hemifields represented in each IC, the commissure may operate to calibrate one with the other.
evidence: This is speculation based on experimental findings.

claim: Stimuli that arrive at each of the two ears are commonly disparate in temporal, level or spectral characteristics.
source: Stimuli that arrive at each of the two ears are commonly disparate in temporal, level or spectral characteristics.
evidence: This is established knowledge about auditory processing.

claim: These disparities are fused by central processing into an auditory percept.
source: These disparities are fused by central processing into an auditory percept.
evidence: This is established knowledge about auditory processing.

claim: Our behavioral sensitivity to changes in sound position is greatest around the midline where the left and right auditory hemi-field representations meet.
source: The construction of left and right auditory hemi-fields is a consequence of monaural and binaural analysis in the brainstem leading to the encoding of sound source location in azimuth and elevation, but our behavioral sensitivity to changes in sound position is greatest around the midline where these representations meet (Mills, 1958).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Our ability to separate sound sources is enhanced by binaural hearing.
source: Furthermore, our ability to separate sound sources, for example to hear out an individual speaker in a noisy social situation, is enhanced by binaural hearing (Litovsky and McAlpine, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Commissural modulation of frequency receptive fields in the ICs may assist sound source separation in acoustically cluttered situations.
source: Commissural modulation of frequency receptive fields in the ICs may assist sound source separation in acoustical cluttered situations.
evidence: This is speculation based on experimental findings.

claim: By modulating the spectral area of FRAs in each IC, commissural processing may increase FRA diversity to overcome correlated noise present in a neural population, and thus improve signal extraction and information content in a neuronal population.
source: By modulating the spectral area of FRAs in each IC, this processing may increase FRA diversity to overcome correlated noise present in a neural population, and thus improve signal extraction and information content in a neuronal population (Zohar et al., 2013).
evidence: This is speculation supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The IC is the first structure where the parallel pathways emerging from the cochlear nucleus can be integrated.
source: It is the first structure where the parallel pathways emerging from the cochlear nucleus (Harrison and Warr, 1962; Osen, 1970; Cant and Benson, 2003) and further elaborated in the brainstem nuclei can be integrated.
evidence: This is an inference based on anatomical knowledge and cited research.

claim: The different cues for determining sound location (interaural time and level disparities and pinna spectral cues) are computed in separate nuclei and are first brought together in the ICs.
source: Thus, the different cues for determining sound location, (interaural time and level disparities and pinna spectral cues) are computed in separate nuclei and are first brought together in the ICs.
evidence: This is an inference based on anatomical and functional knowledge.

claim: Responses to changes in overall sound level at the periphery will always be congruent in the left and right ICs.
source: Responses to changes in overall sound level at the periphery will always be congruent in the left and right ICs, while changes in azimuthal location will produce changes in firing rate in each IC antipodal to the other.
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge of auditory processing.

claim: Changes in azimuthal location will produce changes in firing rate in each IC antipodal to the other.
source: Responses to changes in overall sound level at the periphery will always be congruent in the left and right ICs, while changes in azimuthal location will produce changes in firing rate in each IC antipodal to the other.
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge of auditory processing.

claim: Processing between the ICs likely takes advantage of the symmetrical organization of the CoIC, so that bilateral changes in firing rate in each IC can better represent changes in sound level and location.
source: Processing between the ICs likely takes advantage of the symmetrical organization of the CoIC, so that bilateral changes in firing rate in each IC can better represent changes in sound level and location (Figure 6).
evidence: This is speculation based on experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Commissural processing between the ICs exerts control over the firing rate of most IC neurons.
source: In conclusion, commissural processing between the ICs exerts control over the firing rate of most IC neurons, and contributes to the creation of receptive fields determining responses to two fundamental parameters of sound: frequency and level.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all experimental data.

claim: Commissural processing contributes to the creation of receptive fields determining responses to frequency and level.
source: In conclusion, commissural processing between the ICs exerts control over the firing rate of most IC neurons, and contributes to the creation of receptive fields determining responses to two fundamental parameters of sound: frequency and level.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all experimental data.

claim: Each IC should not be considered as independent of the other, but as two halves of a cooperative whole operating in concert to optimize the encoding of sounds.
source: This degree of interaction suggests that each IC should not be considered as independent of the other, but as two halves of a cooperative whole operating in concert to optimize the encoding of sounds.
evidence: This is an inference based on all experimental data.

claim: Data reported are from experiments performed on 32 (19 male, 13 female) outbred, pigmented guinea pigs (Cavia porcellus).
source: Data reported here are from experiments performed on 32 (19 male, 13 female) outbred, pigmented guinea pigs (Cavia porcellus).
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects.

source: Experimental animals had a median age of 6 months (Inter-quartile range (IQR) = 4 to 7; range = 2 to 13).
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects.
